American Express and Airbnb announced an exclusive partnership in October 2026 that adds over one million Airbnb listings, including Airbnb Luxe, to the Amex Travel platform for eligible U.S. Card Members with new ways to earn Membership Rewards points and statement credits.

The tie up plugs Airbnb into American Express's high spending travel portal, potentially shifting more bookings into premium homes, Airbnb Luxe stays and Experiences, while Card Members still manage trips directly on Airbnb after checkout.

Next, the focus moves to how this new Amex Travel distribution for Airbnb could reshape the investment narrative investors have been using.

Capitalize on the Airbnb and Amex partnership theme by scanning other travel and experience platforms that may be gearing up for similar momentum across 19 high quality undiscovered gems.

Airbnb Investment Narrative Recap

Owning Airbnb stock means believing the platform can keep deepening its role in global travel, across homes, hotels, and Experiences, while preserving strong profitability. The short term swing factor is execution around Q3 2026 results on 5 November, especially nights booked, Experiences traction, and any color on demand into 2027.

The biggest near term risk still sits with regulation and platform disintermediation. Tougher local rules on short term rentals or a shift of bookings toward third party AI agents could weigh on listing supply and direct traffic. The Amex deal helps on demand access but does not remove those structural threats.

The recent American Express partnership looks most relevant because it directly affects distribution and mix. Access to high spending cardholders inside Amex Travel could skew more bookings into higher value categories such as Airbnb Luxe, which matters given investors are watching revenue quality as much as headline growth.

This sits alongside another fresh development: the move to scrap checkout chore lists from 20 November 2026. If the policy improves guest satisfaction without meaningfully hurting host economics, it could support retention and repeat use. Both updates feed into the same catalyst playbook: more engaged users and deeper attachment to the Airbnb ecosystem.

For readers tracking the numbers behind this new Airbnb and American Express link up, analysts are working off a narrative where Airbnb reaches US$18.6b in revenue and US$4.7b in earnings by 2029. This is underpinned by a forecast 12.3% yearly increase in revenue and an earnings step up of about US$2b from current earnings of US$2.7b.

How the Amex Travel deal tests Airbnb's platform story

The big idea behind Airbnb is that a broad travel and living platform can keep adding new ways to book and stay, while still pushing demand back into its core homes marketplace. This American Express tie up plugs directly into that Narrative because it is about distribution power and who owns the guest relationship.

"The main thing that has to go right is that hotels, services and other new travel verticals keep scaling while feeding demand back into core homes, even as regulatory scrutiny and new AI booking agents test Airbnb's ability to retain direct customer relationships..."

The catch is that distribution cuts both ways. Routing bookings through Amex Travel gives Airbnb access to premium customers yet it also tests the thesis that the business can resist powerful intermediaries, especially with AI booking agents and large issuers like American Express or competitors such as Booking Holdings and Expedia vying to sit between guest and host.

Key Takeaways

Every recent price target on Booking Holdings (BKNG:NASDAQ) is above the stock, from Wells Fargo's $190 to UBS's $265, even after a 27% drop this year.

Wall Street's estimates already have Airbnb's (ABNB:NASDAQ) revenue growing faster than Booking's this year and next, so the bear case that Booking is losing share is mostly priced in.

Booking's alternative-accommodation room nights grew faster in Q3, but its Q4 guidance calls for adjusted revenue growth of just 0% to 2%.

The $190 target looks safe. The bigger risk is that the Q4 slowdown pulls down next year's estimates, and Airbnb's Nov. 5 report is the next read.

Booking Holdings is down 28% this year, and Wall Street still can't find a price target anywhere near the stock.

On Tuesday, UBS trimmed its target to $265 from $274 and kept its Buy rating. The lowest of the five recent calls is Wells Fargo's $190 with a Hold, and it's still 22% above the stock's latest close of $155.67.

The bear case is that Airbnband AI search are taking travel demand away from Booking. If that's right, the revenue and earnings estimates behind every one of those targets are too high.

Even the low target is well above the stock

Here are the five calls since Oct. 21, with each target's upside from the latest close:

UBS (Nov. 3): Buy, $265, from $274, 70% upside

Bank of America (Oct. 26): Buy, $232, from $234, 49%

Robert W. Baird (Oct. 27): Buy, $223, from $230, 43%

RBC Capital (Oct. 21): Buy, $220, 41%

Wells Fargo (Oct. 27): Hold, $190, from $220, 22%

Four of the five cut their targets, and Wells Fargo cut the most.

But $190 is still about 18x the $10.46 of normalized EPS analysts expect from Booking this year. The stock trades at about 14x.

So even the cautious call asks for only a slightly higher multiple on earnings Wall Street already expects. That means the targets stand or fall on whether those estimates hold up.

Key Takeaways

Booking Holdings stock is down 27% this year, and UBS, Baird, Bank of America and RBC Capital all kept Buy ratings ahead of its third-quarter report, though most of them trimmed their targets.

Analysts' estimates point to a lower valuation as the cause of the drop: going into the report, consensus had normalized EPS climbing from $9.12 in fiscal 2025 to $14.46 in fiscal 2028.

Booking's third quarter beat its own guidance, with room nights up 7% against a forecast of 3%-5%, though demand softened in October and fourth-quarter guidance calls for room nights up just 1% to 3%.

Booking Holdings (BKNG:NASDAQ) is down 27% this year through its Nov. 3 close, and analysts spent the weeks before its third-quarter report cutting their price targets.

They didn't cut their ratings, though. Four of the five recent calls covered here still say Buy. Then Booking's Nov. 3 report gave them a decent case, even as shares slipped about 1.5% in after-hours trading, according to Reuters.

Smaller targets, same Buy ratings

Here are the calls, newest first:

UBS reiterated its Buy on Nov. 3, hours before the report, and cut its target to $265 from $274.

Baird kept its Outperform rating, its version of a Buy, on Oct. 27 and cut its target to $223 from $230.

Bank of America reiterated its Buy on Oct. 26 and trimmed its target to $232 from $234.

RBC Capital kept its Buy and a $220 target on Oct. 20.

Wells Fargo kept its Equal Weight rating on Oct. 7 and cut its target to $190 from $220.

title: Management Raised the Bar For Expedia Stock; Does The Chart Agree?

Management Raised the Bar For Expedia Stock; Does The Chart Agree?

Expedia (EXPE) raised its revenue forecast for fiscal 2026 on August 5, 2026, yet the stock has slipped 6.3% from its August 5 close, the last before that after-market release, through November 2, against a 2.4% fall for the S&P 500. A higher forecast alongside a weaker share price is a mixed signal, and the chart is worth checking before taking the raise at face value. So where does Expedia's share price stand today against its own averages?

Expedia Stock Backs The Raise Only In Part

Expedia's share price stands above both of its main averages. The stock closed at $298.99 on November 2, above its 50-day average of $285.69, the average closing price over the last 50 trading days. That 50-day average sits above the 200-day average of $258.50, the same measure over 200 trading days, leaving the stock's uptrend intact on its averages.

The stock's return since the release does not align with the raise. Expedia reported after the market closed on August 5. On August 6, the first session after the release, the stock fell 4.1% while the S&P 500 slipped 0.2%, a move that priced the second-quarter results and the raised forecast together. Much of the strength above the averages is recent: over the month to November 2, Expedia stock returned 12.8%, including dividends, against a 2.3% loss for the S&P 500.

What Expedia Raised For Fiscal 2026

Management raised its fiscal 2026 revenue forecast to a range of $16.05 billion to $16.22 billion. At the midpoint, that is 2.1% above the $15.8 billion it guided in May. Management tied the raise to the strength of the first half and its assumptions for the third quarter.

That strength showed in the second quarter, when revenue grew 14% from a year earlier, a pace management said beat its own expectations. The business-to-business segment, which serves more than 70,000 partners, posted its 20th straight quarter of double-digit growth.

The raise went beyond revenue. Management lifted its fiscal 2026 forecast for gross bookings, the value of travel booked through Expedia, to $130 billion at the midpoint from $128 billion. It also now expects its adjusted EBITDA margin, its own measure of earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization as a share of revenue, to widen by 1.6 percentage points over last year at the midpoint, up from 1.1 points.

What Could Move Expedia Stock From Here?

A much slower second half would still meet the raised forecast. At its midpoint, the raised forecast leaves Expedia needing about $8.39 billion in the third and fourth quarters of fiscal 2026, or 5.5% more than in the same quarters a year earlier. That compares with 14.3% growth in the first half. For the third quarter, management guided revenue growth of about 5% to 8% and said it expects bookings growth to moderate as Expedia laps faster growth from a year earlier.

Airbnb ABNB is set to report its third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 5.

For the third quarter of 2026, Airbnb expects revenues between $4.69 billion and $4.77 billion, implying growth of 15-17%.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for third-quarter 2026 revenues is pegged at $4.75 billion, suggesting an increase of 15.98% from the year-ago quarter's reported figure.

The consensus mark for third-quarter 2026 earnings is pegged at $2.89 per share, which has been unchanged over the past 30 days. This indicates 30.77% year-over-year growth.

Airbnb, Inc. Price and EPS Surprise
Airbnb, Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

Airbnb, Inc. price-eps-surprise | Airbnb, Inc. Quote

The company's earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate in one of the trailing four quarters while missing on three occasions, with the negative average surprise being 5.15%.

Let's see how things have shaped up prior to this announcement.

Factors Likely to Have Impacted ABNB's Q3 Performance

Airbnb's third-quarter 2026 performance is expected to have benefited from strong global travel demand, accelerating bookings, improving average daily rates (ADR) and continued momentum across its core and expansion markets. In the to-be-reported quarter, the company expects gross booking value to grow in the mid-teens year over year, driven by low double-digit growth in Nights and Seats Booked and a moderate increase in ADR, supported by favorable business mix and price appreciation.

The company is likely to have benefited from strong demand across North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia Pacific. Expansion markets, particularly India and Brazil, are expected to have supported growth through increasing adoption among first-time bookers. Improving demand across established markets, including the United States, France, the United Kingdom and Australia, is likely to have strengthened booking volumes.

The company's ongoing investments in artificial intelligence (AI)-powered product enhancements are expected to have improved booking conversion rates in the to-be-reported quarter. Better search and discovery, personalized recommendations, AI-generated listing and review highlights and simplified checkout processes are likely to have enhanced user engagement. The expansion of Reserve Now, Pay Later and simplified service fees is expected to have supported booking growth, improved affordability and strengthened host competitiveness.

Airbnb's expanding hotel inventory is likely to have contributed to growth in the to-be-reported quarter. Hotel nights grew approximately three times faster than home nights in the second quarter, reflecting strong demand. The expansion of Airbnb Services, including car rentals, grocery delivery, airport pickup and luggage storage, alongside growing Experiences offerings, is expected to have supported customer engagement and platform adoption.

However, Airbnb's third-quarter 2026 performance is likely to have been hurt by higher investments in product development, artificial intelligence and sales and marketing initiatives. Increased spending on business expansion and customer incentives, alongside tougher year-over-year comparisons, is expected to have pressured margins. The company anticipates a slight year-over-year decline in adjusted EBITDA margin due to the timing of investment.

Airbnb: Seasonal Fluctuations in Its Quarterly Revenue

Airbnb Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) primarily generates its revenue by operating a global digital marketplace that directly connects independent hosts offering a wide variety of accommodations and unique local experiences with guests seeking temporary lodging options across the globe.

It recently introduced new artificial intelligence tools designed for dynamic property pricing while updating its global house rules policy and launching an exclusive travel booking partnership directly with American Express.

Chewy: Gradual Upward Trends in Quarterly Revenue

Chewy Inc. (NYSE:CHWY) primarily earns its revenue by functioning as an online retail enterprise that provides essential pet food, prescribed medications, and general health and wellness supplies to domestic companion owners across the United States.

It recently updated the annual fee and rewards structure of its paid membership program and expanded its physical operational footprint by hosting an open house for a new veterinary clinic located in Colorado.

Foolish Take

Normally, the first thing to note when examining a company's revenue trend is seasonality: some times of the year have stronger buying patterns than others. For most stocks, compare revenue year over year, by quarter. In normal times, seasonality holds true for consumer stocks like these as well. Airbnb gets exceptional volume for summer months in the Northern Hemisphere, which translates into third-quarter revenue being booked. Chewy has less seasonality, generally around the Christmas season like most retailers. The strength of its autoship program mitigates seasonality; however, one would expect its increasing focus on veterinary services to smooth out seasonality as well.
